decision: Preserve the user review bundle before policy work
why: The staged review files are unrelated user work and must survive the session byte-for-byte
result: Worktree contains only pre-existing untracked files; Bead claimed safely

decision: Start with the missing lifecycle policy as a failing contract
why: The current integer approval list cannot prove stable requirements, deprecation windows, or channel rules
evidence: python3 test/test_semver_lifecycle_policy.py: 3 missing-file errors and old analyzer-option failure
result: Red baseline proves the machine checklist, human policy, and release wiring do not yet exist

decision: Replace the raw stable-major integer list with a small reviewed release-line checklist
why: A number can permit 1.0 but cannot explain which readiness requirements passed or who approved the promise
result: The analyzer derives approved majors only from complete requirements plus an explicit dated commit-pinned approval

decision: Point release policy at the compatibility maturity authority instead of repeating beta state
why: Product maturity and SemVer lineage answer different questions; duplicating beta creates drift
result: Release policy owns channel mechanics while compatibility evidence remains the sole maturity authority

decision: Enforce channel deprecation experimental and stable-approval invariants with mutation tests
why: Governance text is not sufficient if CI accepts a prerelease channel shortened deprecation or incomplete stable approval
evidence: python3 test/test_semver_lifecycle_policy.py; npm run test:release-version-policy; npm run release:policy
result: Focused policy contracts pass and known bypass mutations fail closed

decision: Reject format-only stable approvals and bind them to real unchanged reviewed source history
why: The first validator accepted any 40-hex value and therefore did not prove the documented commit pin
evidence: xhigh second-pass finding 1; temporary-Git approval source binding test
result: Approval SHA must exist and be ancestral; only release/policy.json and .beads/interactions.jsonl may differ afterward

decision: Close analyzer and schema loopholes found after the initial green result
why: The earlier green row proved constant drift rejection but did not yet prove commit-scope floors or reject every unknown authority field
evidence: xhigh second-pass findings 2 and 3; fix(experimental) and fix(deprecation) mapping tests; exact-key mutation tests
result: Experimental and deprecation scopes now have a minor floor and every policy object rejects undeclared keys

decision: Limit approval freshness to the major transition and block unproved stable experimental minors
why: Rechecking a historical approval on every stable patch would freeze the admitted line while an unconditional experimental scope would bypass the proof rule
evidence: xhigh re-review findings 1 and 2; stable maintenance and stable experimental rejection tests
result: Major-transition approval is checked once; ordinary stable maintenance proceeds; stable experimental minors fail until proof machinery exists

decision: Restrict reviewed-policy drift to the target approval field
why: Allowing any release/policy.json edit after review could change channel or admission semantics under the same approval
evidence: temporary-Git policy-drift mutation test; deep comparison with reviewed release/policy.json
result: The reviewed policy must be identical except that the target approval changes from null to its validated record

decision: Accept the remediated xhigh design after independent read-only re-review
why: The final review found no blocker or high issue after transition-scoped freshness experimental proof rejection and exact policy-delta checks
evidence: trail_audit final review; no blocker/high findings; residual noncanonical policyPath risk is excluded by official config verification
result: Second-pass requirement satisfied with no unresolved material finding

decision: Run focused downstream changed-file release and full compiler gates
why: The policy touches release automation and shared documentation so both direct contracts and repository-wide regression evidence are required
evidence: npm run test:release-contracts; npm run test:changed; npm test; compatibility:verify; 301 snapshot summary
result: All gates passed; 301 snapshots passed with zero failures
